why_not_layout: image_fingerprint.py's layout hashes the defined-symbol address map. It answers 'is this the same image' and cannot answer 'would this execute the same instructions': two xPack 15.2.1 builds with different layout have identical code, because the bundled newlib and libgcc archives are separate builds in the darwin-x64 and win32-x64 packages.

within_bench_after_55.what: Track A vs Track B, one bench, one commit, one compiler
within_bench_after_55.means: A-vs-B has no oracle power on shared source now. Not reduced - none. This is the axis cmake/track_a.cmake's header predicted would be destroyed by aligning the toolchains.

across_toolchains.what: ARM GNU 14.3.1 vs xPack 15.2.1, Track B, one commit
across_toolchains.means: The codegen axis did not disappear, it moved from within a bench to between benches. frame_crc32_update and the stream_core pair are the wire contract and the framer seam.

cross_host_same_release.predicted_by: mac-bench, on #54, before either of us looked
cross_host_same_release.means: One xPack release generates byte-identical code on two host OSes. So the project has TWO code generators, not three: ARM GNU 14.3.1 and xPack 15.2.1, the latter wearing two hostnames.

corrects: windows-desk posted 'four builds of one commit, four layouts' on #5 and read it as four draws. It is three layouts' worth of bookkeeping over two code generators - counting layouts and reporting them as code generators.
not_claimed: that the single-knob #5 result is affected - it compared ARM GNU 14.3.1 against xPack 15.2.1, which are genuinely different code
that layout is useless - it answers the flash log's question
that the shared-source function list is complete; it is textual and a lower bound, 72 candidates and 64 found in both images

generator_partition_settled.method: all 18 differing shared-source functions hashed on each install and compared mechanically, no ELF shared between benches
generator_partition_settled.count: four builds, four layouts, TWO generators, THREE installs
generator_partition_settled.resolves: linux-x1's objection to the single-knob wording. Their bench and windows-desk have the SAME generated code, so their site sets agreeing at 0.862 is 'same codegen, same site set' - the table is consistent and nothing needs narrowing. Their #5 cross-bench agreement was a genuine bench-to-bench comparison with the code held fixed, which is what the pinned experiment was trying to buy.
generator_partition_settled.fragility: The axis is 14.x against 15.x and nothing protects it. windows-desk is the only bench with both installed - ARM GNU 14.3.1 as the registry default, xPack 15.2.1 opt-in outside the registry globs - so it otherwise rests on mac-bench staying on xPack and linux-x1 on Debian's 14.2.1, neither of which was decided for that reason.
generator_partition_settled.the_catch: Sizes and instruction counts see two generators as one: ten of the 18 differ at identical length, frame_crc32_update among them at 16 on both. Layouts see one generator as two: the xPack pair differ in layout and not in code. Only the instruction sequence gets it right, and both errors were made on this issue by people who had written the tool.
